question.worked_solution:
The cardinality of a finite set $A$ is the number of elements in $A.$ 

Notice that the elements of our set 

$$
3,\,18,\,108,\,648,\,…
$$

form a geometric sequence with a common ratio $r=6:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =6 \\  & =\frac{18}{3} \\  & =\frac{108}{18} \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

The $n$th term of our geometric sequence, denoted ${a}_{n},$ is given by

$$
{a}_{n}={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1}=3({6}^{n-1})=\frac{1}{2}(6)^{n}.
$$

Therefore, we can express $A$ in set-builder notation as follows:

$$
A=\{\frac{1}{2}(6)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le N\}
$$

where $N\in N$ is to be determined.

To find $N,$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}(6)^{N} & =181\,398\,528 \\ {6}^{N} & =362\,797\,056 \\ N & ={log}_{6}⁡(362\,797\,056) \\ N & =\frac{{log}_{10}⁡(362\,797\,056)}{{log}_{10}⁡(6)} \\ N & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ can be expressed as

$$
A=\{\frac{1}{2}(6)^{n}:n\in N,\,1\le n\le 11\}.
$$

Finally, since $A$ has $11$ elements, we must have $|A|=11.$
